ladder.teaches: converging pointers on a sorted array (pair sum)
ladder.why: The canonical first rung: on a sorted array, a sum that is too small can only be fixed by moving the left pointer, too big only by moving the right one.
Two pointers walking inward compare mirror characters, with skipping of non-alphanumerics showing how each pointer can move on its own rule.

ladder.teaches: reader and writer pointers (compact in place)
ladder.why: A reader scans everything while a writer marks the end of the kept prefix: the template for every in-place compaction.
Merging two sorted runs with one pointer each, and filling from the back so the in-place merge never overwrites unread values.

ladder.teaches: move the side that cannot improve (container)
ladder.why: Why discarding the shorter line is safe: it can never do better with a narrower partner, the argument behind every opposite-ends squeeze.

ladder.teaches: fix one element, two-pointer the rest, skip duplicates (3Sum)
ladder.why: Sorting turns 3Sum into n runs of sorted Two Sum, and duplicate-skipping on both the fixed index and the left pointer gives each triplet once.
The two ends of a sorted array with negatives are two sorted sequences of squares; comparing the ends and writing from the back is an O(n) merge.

ladder.teaches: converging pointers on a sorted array (pair sum)
ladder.why: Amazon OA: pair sum at most a capacity across two lists, where an overflowing background app is useless for every larger foreground app, plus collecting ties.
Amazon OA: after sorting both arrays, each frontend takes the smallest backend it beats, a greedy that is really two sequences walked together.

ladder.teaches: fix one element, two-pointer the rest, skip duplicates (3Sum)
ladder.why: Counting instead of listing: once a[lo] + a[hi] fits the budget, every hi' between lo and hi fits too, so add hi - lo in one step.
Mirror-pair comparison applied block by block, where each mismatched pair costs exactly one change.
The first mismatch is the only decision point: one of the two characters must go, so check both remaining middles.

ladder.teaches: fix one element, two-pointer the rest, skip duplicates (3Sum)
ladder.why: The 3Sum scan without an exact target: the same pointer moves now chase the smallest distance to target.

ladder.teaches: move the side that cannot improve (container)
ladder.why: The side with the smaller running max already knows its water level, so settle it and move it: the container argument with an insight.

notes: All six techniques have a clean classic. The bank has no plain Remove Duplicates beyond GEP's (used) and Move Zeroes / Sort Colors (bloomberg-move-zeroes, bloomberg-sort-colors) are good extra reader/writer drills outside any pool if a second compaction rung is wanted. salesforce-minimum-removals-to-balance-array and amazon-get-minimum-boxes are same-direction windows, so they fit sliding-window better.
